questions.question_text: Which of these numbers could be the probability of an event?

options.why: A probability can never be greater than $1$, because no event is more likely than certain.
A probability can never be less than $0$, because no event is less likely than impossible.
A probability must lie between $0$ and $1$; $6.5$ is far outside the scale.

questions.solution_text:
Every probability satisfies $0 \le P(\text{event}) \le 1$.
$1.3$, $-0.4$ and $6.5$ all lie outside this range.
Only $0.85$ could be a probability.

questions.question_text: An event has a probability of $0$. What does this tell you about the event?

options.why: A certain event has probability $1$, at the top of the scale, not $0$.
An unlikely event has a probability between $0$ and $\frac{1}{2}$; a probability of exactly $0$ means it never happens.

options.text: The event has an even chance
options.why: An even chance means a probability of exactly $\frac{1}{2}$, not $0$.

questions.solution_text:
A probability of $0$ sits at the very bottom of the scale.
The event never happens — it is impossible.

questions.question_text: Which word best describes the event 'the sun rises tomorrow morning'?

options.why: Likely means more than half the time but not always; the sun rises every morning, so the event always happens.
An even chance means the event happens exactly half the time, but the sun rises every morning.
Impossible means the event never happens, but the sun rises every morning.

questions.solution_text:
The sun rises every morning, so the event always happens.
It is certain, with a probability of $1$.

questions.question_text: A standard six-sided die is rolled. Which word best describes the event 'rolling an even number'?

options.why: Likely means more than half the outcomes are favourable, but exactly $3$ of the $6$ outcomes are even — exactly half.
Unlikely means less than half the outcomes are favourable, but $3$ of the $6$ outcomes are even — exactly half.
Certain means the event always happens, but rolling an odd number is also possible.

questions.solution_text:
The even numbers on the die are $\{2, 4, 6\}$ — exactly $3$ of the $6$ equally likely outcomes.
$P(\text{even}) = \frac{1}{2}$, which is exactly half, so the event is an even chance.

Arrow $C$ sits between $\frac{1}{2}$ and $1$, so it shows a likely event.
Arrow $D$ sits at exactly $1$, so it shows a certain event.

questions.solution_text:
An unlikely event has a probability between $0$ and $\frac{1}{2}$, and 'not impossible' means it is above $0$.
Arrow $A$ is the only arrow strictly between $0$ and $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.question_text: A jar contains $5$ red, $6$ yellow and $2$ blue lollies. One lolly is picked at random. What is the value of $P(\text{red}) + P(\text{yellow}) + P(\text{blue})$?

options.why: This leaves out one lolly; all $13$ lollies are red, yellow or blue, so the numerators add to $13$.
This counts the $3$ colours over the $13$ lollies; instead, add the three probabilities themselves.
This adds the numbers of lollies, not their probabilities; each probability is a fraction out of $13$.

questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{red}) + P(\text{yellow}) + P(\text{blue}) = \frac{5}{13} + \frac{6}{13} + \frac{2}{13}$
$= \frac{13}{13}$
$= 1$
The probabilities of all the outcomes always add to $1$.

questions.question_text: A jar contains only red, yellow and blue lollies. For one lolly picked at random, $P(\text{red}) = 0.45$ and $P(\text{yellow}) = 0.3$. What is $P(\text{blue})$, as a decimal?

options.why: This is $P(\text{red}) + P(\text{yellow})$; the missing probability is $1$ minus this total.
This subtracts only $P(\text{red})$ from $1$ and forgets to subtract $P(\text{yellow})$.
This subtracts only $P(\text{yellow})$ from $1$ and forgets to subtract $P(\text{red})$.

questions.solution_text:
The probabilities of all the outcomes add to $1$.
$P(\text{blue}) = 1 - 0.45 - 0.3$
$= 0.25$

questions.question_text: A jar contains only red, yellow and blue lollies. For one lolly picked at random, $P(\text{red}) = \frac{2}{5}$ and $P(\text{yellow}) = \frac{1}{4}$. What is $P(\text{blue})$, as a fraction?

options.why: Adds the two given probabilities with the correct common denominator, $\frac{8}{20} + \frac{5}{20}$, but stops there instead of subtracting that total from $1$.
Subtracts from $1$ correctly but adds the two fractions by adding numerators and denominators, getting $\frac{3}{9}$, so $1 - \frac{3}{9} = \frac{6}{9}$.
Adds numerators and denominators separately to get $\frac{3}{9}$ and also forgets to subtract that total from $1$.

questions.solution_text:
The probabilities of all the outcomes add to $1$.
$P(\text{blue}) = 1 - \frac{2}{5} - \frac{1}{4}$
$= \frac{20}{20} - \frac{8}{20} - \frac{5}{20}$
$= \frac{7}{20}$

questions.question_text: A jar contains only red, yellow and blue lollies, and one lolly is picked at random. Which set of numbers could be the probabilities of the three colours?
